 Enter fullscreen mode displaying this image. Expand Your daily lunchtime read. WATCH | ‘Players were tense under Broos’ — Benni lauds Pitso’s Bafana 
 Kenya coach Benni McCaarthy during their training ahead of their match with Bafana Bafana on Friday. Kenya coach and Bafana Bafana legend Benni McCarthy is of the strong view that SA would have gone even further at the last World Cup under incumbent mentor Pitso Mosimane.
 McCarthy, whose Kenya face Bafana in Group D of the qualifiers for next year’s Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) at Orlando Amstel Arena on Friday at 6pm, feels players are playing with freedom under Mosimane, compared to his predecessor Hugo Broos, who guided SA to the last 32 of the recent global spectacle co-hosted by the US, Mexico and Canada a few months ago.
 Bafana Bafana legend and Kenya coach Benni McCarthy says Bafana now play with freedom under coach Pitso Mosimane, asserting that they would have gone further at the World Cup if Mosimane was in charge. Get the full story here: https://t.co/8hBhwbOTGQ

 How Njerae turned heartbreak into a hit 
 Kenyan singer Njerae wants to take over the African diaspora. When Kenyan singer Njerae, real name Njeri Mwengi, released the hit Aki Sioni , she had no idea her heartbreak story would connect with music lovers around the globe.
 The Nairobi-born singer blends Afro-indie, contemporary R&B and soul. With more than six million streams, the track turned her into a household name.

 Kaytranada returns to SA to round off 2026, Olivia Dean to set the tone for 2027 
 Kaytranada. Pic. REUTERS/Mario Anzuoni Grammy-winning superstar Kaytranada is returning to SA next month to kick off the vibes for the third annual Milk + Cookies festival.
 The producer headlined the inaugural festival in 2025 and performed at Afropunk Joburg in 2019. Now he will perform at:
 Kenilworth, Cape Town, on December 18; and
 Nasrec in Johannesburg on December 20.
